TITLE: The 2009 male-intensive employment collapse
EXPLANATION: The 2009 male-intensive employment collapse. The male share of household primary income fell in 23 of the 26 countries in 2009; LT (-6.70 points) and LV (-3.50) are the two largest falls, ahead of IE (-2.86), BG (-2.44) and EE (-1.93). The move sits in employment income (LT dY -6.70 against dYE -6.54), and the pension flows scaled off that shape move with it by an identical -0.065. The mirror image is on the benefit side, where the male share rises as men move onto benefits (LT B +17.1 points, LV B +9.7). It unwinds gradually rather than snapping back: LT 49.49 (2009), 49.65, 50.91, 51.95, 52.22, 53.11 (2014). Same event as the EU-wide 2009 recession rules already in the ledger, which cover the level tier only. Bug report #218. Scan triage 2026-09-18.

TITLE: Slovakia moves opposite to the other four countries flagged for TXH in 2022 (+1.57 pp of household primary income, z +2.72, against falls of 0.31 to 1.34 elsewhere), so the EU relief story does not apply to it
EXPLANATION: Slovakia moves opposite to the other four countries flagged for TXH in 2022 (+1.57 pp of household primary income, z +2.72, against falls of 0.31 to 1.34 elsewhere), so the EU relief story does not apply to it. Slovakia was withdrawing household support in this window rather than adding it. Ministry of Finance SR, Institute for Financial Policy, Policy brief 2022/7 'How did high inflation come about?', 16 June 2022 (https://www.mfsr.sk/files/archiv/47/Policy_brief_Inflation_2022.pdf) documents three measures pointing the same way: free school meals in primary schools were CANCELLED from September 2021, contributing 0.5 pp to inflation in the first month and affecting year-on-year rates until August 2022; tobacco excise rose from 1 February 2021 (0.3 pp) with a further round from March 2022 (0.1 pp); and the nominal value of pensions, material-need benefits, parental allowance and child allowance is indexed to the PREVIOUS year's inflation, so the 2022 spike only reaches those transfers in 2023, temporarily reducing their value. The brief records no offsetting Slovak household relief package as of June 2022. INTERPRETATION, not established: the brief describes benefits and excise duties, not the D7 other-current-transfers item TXH is built from, so the direction is explained but the exact mechanism is not traced. Triaged 2026-09-23.

TITLE: TFPO RO 2019: household TPSOCfc 2017 1,889, 2018 1,752, 2019 3,167, 2020 2,853 mio EUR (1.01, 0.86, 1.42, 1.30% of GDP), +81% in 2019 and stays high
EXPLANATION: TFPO RO 2019: household TPSOCfc 2017 1,889, 2018 1,752, 2019 3,167, 2020 2,853 mio EUR (1.01, 0.86, 1.42, 1.30% of GDP), +81% in 2019 and stays high. Funded pensions, published-aggregate discontinuity, not a profile or metric artefact. TFPI and TFPO are the household BPSOCfc and TPSOCfc (identical in all years). Not traced to the raw Eurostat series here; which reform or contribution-rate change produced the step is not established and not asserted. DX-11 triage 2026-09-25.

TITLE: Source-tracked, level not reproduced exactly
EXPLANATION: Source-tracked, level not reproduced exactly. BROW is the sum over sectors of net current transfers from the rest of the world. Rebuilt from the S2 items of nasa_10_nf_tr (D51, D59, D61, D62, D71, D72, D74, D75, D29 received and paid) the year-on-year change follows the published one; the LEVEL differs by the items that table does not carry (D76, taxes on production, the payroll-tax adjustment), so no exact identity is claimed.

TITLE: TROW (Government) equals the NTA profile TGNF in every year (762 country-years checked) and is -BROW of the government sector by construction
EXPLANATION: TROW (Government) equals the NTA profile TGNF in every year (762 country-years checked) and is -BROW of the government sector by construction. The government's share of the rest-of-world flows cannot be separated in nasa_10_nf_tr, so the check is against the S2 net from ROW for the whole economy: the government's published change moves in the same direction and by a similar amount,.

TITLE: German EU-SILC age bands (2022-2023) and top-coding at 73 (2014-2018)
EXPLANATION: In DE 2022 and 2023 every SILC-based profile is a step function over the age bands 16-19, 20-24, ..., 75-79 of the source (in 2014-2018 top-coded at 73). A known source limitation (bug report, DE alpha special case; #223/#224; Limitations.tex, Germany). The steps make single ages at the band edges look like spikes and kinks, and the bands themselves show as plateaus. Decided: the steps are kept, not smoothed across band mid-points (#249).

TITLE: No household/NPISH split in the ESA source
EXPLANATION: For DE 2008-2011 and IE 2008-2009 the ESA 2010 sector accounts publish households and NPISH only combined (S14_S15), so the NPISH part of other current transfers, TXNPISH, does not exist in the source and is absent from the published aggregates. Source data, known to the project owner (2026-09-25).

TITLE: BG 2023 not published
EXPLANATION: Eurostat has no BG 2023 sector accounts, so BG 2023 stays missing in every file (project convention, CLAUDE.md).

TITLE: HR 2008 has no age profiles
EXPLANATION: No EU-SILC based profiles exist for HR 2008 - the published files correctly start in 2009 (bug report, HR 2009-2010 entry: 'HR 2008 is correctly absent'). The household TB split (TBSN, TBPPEN) is blank in 2008 as well, where there is no EUROMOD decomposition (#237).

TITLE: BG other social benefits zero in 2009, 2010 and 2015
EXPLANATION: COFOG reports nothing for GF1006-GF1009 in 2009 and 2015 (TOTAL = GF10, residual -0.1 floored to 0), and the neighbouring years are 0.2-10.4 mio EUR, so BSX genuinely lives at zero (#233 B). The NTA copy TGICX is missing in those years rather than zero; left alone as a sector-consistency question (bug report, DX-06 entry).

TITLE: No funded-pension benefits paid yet (BG, RO)
EXPLANATION: Household BPSOCfc (funded pensions received) is 0 in the published aggregates for BG in every year and for RO until 2011 (RO pays 1, 2, 3, 5 mio EUR from 2012 on; checked 2026-09-25). With nothing received, the NTA funded-pension inflow TFPI is missing and the RO BPSOCfc profile is zero in those years.

TITLE: Baltic GDP collapse 2009
EXPLANATION: Nominal GDP fell by 15.0% in EE, 17.5% in LT and 21.2% in LV in 2009, and LV fell a further 4.5% in 2010 (published aggregates, checked 2026-09-25) - the three largest falls in the EU. Level breaks are scored as shares of GDP, so every item that did not fall in proportion shows a break in 2009, and many revert or overshoot in 2010. The flags are the denominator plus the recession itself (employment and property income down, transfers and social benefits up).

TITLE: Enrolment definitions changed (ISCED 1997 to ISCED 2011)
EXPLANATION: The enrolment input switches from ISCED 1997 (educ_enrl1tl, until 2012) to ISCED 2011 (educ_uoe_enra02, from 2013) (Suppl_enrollment_educ.do:20-21), and what counts as pre-primary changed with it. In the early years public education consumption at pre-school ages differs from later years: NL age 3 about 100 EUR per person in 2008-2010 against 5,479 from 2011, IE at 5 and PL at 6 in 2008-2009. Not easy to fix; kept as it is (project owner, 2026-09-25).

TITLE: EE funded pensions: source values kept
EXPLANATION: Eurostat reports D62 paid by EE financial corporations as -27, -59, -76, -71, -81 mio EUR in 2013-2017, a hard 0 in 2018 (not a blank: the stored table keeps blanks as missing) and -74 in 2019 - the only negative cells in the table (DX-03, bug report #247). Household BPSOCfc passes these through; in 2018 the profile is zero and NTA TFPI is missing. The project owner decided to keep the source values (2026-09-26).

TITLE: COVID health consumption cycle 2020-2023
EXPLANATION: Government health consumption (CGH) as a share of GDP rose in 26 of 26 countries in 2020, rose further in 18 of 26 in 2021 (median +0.13 pp), fell in 25 of 26 in 2022 and in 16 of 25 in 2023 (published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26). The 2021 and 2023 flags are the tail of that cycle.

TITLE: Tax revenue rebound in 2021
EXPLANATION: Government taxes (T) as a share of GDP fell in 24 of 26 countries in 2020 and rose in 16 of 26 in 2021 (median +0.45 pp; published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26): the rebound after the COVID year.

TITLE: Household property income rising 2021-2023
EXPLANATION: Household property income YP as a share of GDP rose in 19 of 26 countries in 2021 and in 2022 and in 16 of 25 in 2023 (median growth +15%, +18%, +14%; published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26) - dividends and, from 2022, interest rates. The flags covered are all increases.

TITLE: DK corporate income peak in 2022 and fall in 2023
EXPLANATION: Corporate primary income was 49.0, 65.4 and 43.0 bn EUR in 2021-2023 (+33%, then -34%) while GDP rose 10.8% in 2022 and fell only 1.9% in 2023; corporate saving fell 43% in 2023. With corporate income out of the denominator, household income, consumption, taxes and depreciation all rise as a share of GDP in 2023. Numbers from the published aggregates; the cause (a profit swing, plausibly shipping) is not established from the data.

TITLE: NL corporate income dip in 2020 and doubling in 2021
EXPLANATION: Corporate primary income was 83.2, 58.0 and 128.8 bn EUR in 2019-2021 (-30%, +122%), corporate and total-economy saving follow (published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26). Source data; the cause is not established from the data.

TITLE: HU corporate income dip in 2012
EXPLANATION: Corporate primary income was 5.6, 3.3 and 6.6 bn EUR in 2011-2013 (-41%, +101%), total-economy saving 3.1 -> 7.2 bn in 2013 (published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26). Source data; the cause is not established from the data.

TITLE: SK corporate income collapse in 2022
EXPLANATION: Corporate primary income was 6.2, 4.0 and 11.6 bn EUR in 2021-2023 and corporate disposable income turned negative in 2022 (-1.5 bn) before recovering to 6.9 bn in 2023; private saving follows (published aggregates, checked 2026-09-26). Source data; the cause is not established from the data.

TITLE: EE funded-pension reform 2021
EXPLANATION: Household funded pensions received (BPSOCfc) jump from 54 to 219 mio EUR in 2021 while contributions (TPSOCfc) fall from 389 to 220, so net funded pensions BPPEN go from -335 to about 0 (published aggregates). Consistent with the 2021 Estonian second-pillar reform (pillar made voluntary, withdrawals allowed); the reform itself is not checked against source metadata.

TITLE: BG rest-of-world transfers and the 2009 saving swing
EXPLANATION: Other current transfers received from abroad (S2 D75 paid) double in 2010 (947 -> 1,894 mio EUR) and halve in 2014 (2,215 -> 1,068), which moves BROW and NTA TFB; compensation of employees from abroad (S2 D1 paid) falls 604 -> 426 -> 290 in 2008-2010 (YEROW). Private saving SF turns from -577 to +3,417 in 2009: net saving of S11 737 -> 2,279, S12 225 -> 960, households -1,539 -> +178. Household T falls 16% in 2009 while income taxes and contributions (S14_S15 D5, D61) stay flat - the fall is in consumption taxes in the recession. Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: EL rest-of-world transfers 2013 and compensation 2015
EXPLANATION: Other current transfers received from abroad (S2 D7 paid) spike in 2013 (2,215 -> 4,552 -> 2,176 mio EUR), which moves BROW; compensation of employees paid to non-residents (S2 D1 received) jumps 590 -> 1,425 in 2015 (YEROW). Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: LU taxes on products 2015 (VAT on e-services)
EXPLANATION: Taxes on products (S1 D21 paid) fall 16% in 2015 (5,712 -> 4,791 mio EUR); TPSp = D21 paid - D31 received reproduces exactly (4,605). 2015 is the year the EU moved VAT on electronic services to the consumer's country. Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: SE taxes on products and corporate transfers
EXPLANATION: TPSp = D21 paid - D31 received reproduces exactly in 2009, 2011 and 2016 (moves of -9%, +7%, +6%). Corporate BPB follows other current transfers paid by non-financial corporations (S11 D75 paid 3,166 -> 4,494 mio EUR in 2012, 5,623 -> 8,046 in 2022, 6,499 in 2023; 5,185 -> 6,214 in 2019 moves NTA TFB); the cause is not established from the data. Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: AT income tax reform 2016
EXPLANATION: Household current taxes on income and wealth (S14_S15 D5 paid) fall 9%, 40,482 -> 36,772 mio EUR, in 2016 and D51 by 10% - the 2016 Austrian income tax reform. TB (taxes on benefits, a share of income taxes) and household T follow; government T is flat as a share of a growing GDP. Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: PT funded pensions and taxes 2010-2013
EXPLANATION: Household funded pensions received (BPSOCfc) follow D62 paid by S12: 2,517, 2,039, 2,618, 2,040, 1,653 mio EUR in 2009-2013; BPPEN follows. Government current taxes on income (S13 D5 received) rise 10% in 2011 and 28% in 2013 (14,995 -> 19,254) - the 2013 income tax increase. Household other current transfers paid (S14_S15 D75 paid) rise 41% in 2012 (2,847 -> 4,001), which moves TX. Checked 2026-09-26 against nasa_10_nf_tr (CP_MEUR): the published aggregates reproduce the source.

TITLE: Single level breaks checked against their source
EXPLANATION: Each covered flag is one series in one country-year. Each was compared on 2026-09-26 with the source item it is built from (nasa_10_nf_tr, gov_10a_exp, nama_10_co3_p3 in CP_MEUR, or the DG TAXUD tax revenue data): in every case the source moves the same way, so the break is source data. The NOTE of each scope row gives the numbers.

TITLE: Male-share moves from the EU-SILC sex profiles
EXPLANATION: The split between men and women comes from the EU-SILC sex profiles; adjustgender only scales both sexes to the total at each age. Checked 2026-09-26 against the pre-adjustment profiles in ENTA_ageprofiles/ageprofiles (inc, ben): for every directly driven flag the same male-share move is already in the SILC profile, passed through almost exactly (BSU, BSX, YEM) or dampened (YP, because YPr and YPp are scaled separately). The other flags follow one of those drivers, or are net series whose male share is unstable. The NOTE of each scope row gives the numbers.

TITLE: Saving steps at the pension age
EXPLANATION: Saving by age steps at the pension age, where labour income stops and pensions start: BE 2018 from -351 EUR at 65 to +1,237 at 66 (BSPEN +3,700 between 65 and 66); FI 2010-2011 a dip at 63, FI's earliest old-age pension age. The size of the step varies with the SILC sample; the mechanism is the one in #273.
